_comment: Prepared, not run (ADR 0005 rule 5): every number below is computed by tests/test_selection_probe.py from skillc/cost_estimate.py and evals/selection-probe/cases.json, not hand-typed. A future change to the case count, arm count, repeat schedule or token/price assumptions that forgets to update this file is caught by that test.

subscription_login_ruling.scope: covers agent runs (this probe's treatment/baseline attempts) only, via the operator's normal Codex subscription login (the normal rotating OAuth login, never a long-lived key) - not judge calls, which use provider API keys and stay dollar-metered. This probe enables no judge tier, so no dollar-metered spend is estimated below at all.

client_login.codex: operator's normal Codex CLI subscription login (OAuth), not a pay-per-use API key

subscription_login_ruling.prerequisite: the in-container credential path for a subscription-login agent run (skillc/credential.py, docker_backend.DockerBackend.deliver_home_file/read_home_file, issue #98) is now built; this manifest states the ruling and relabels the estimate, it did not itself deliver that prerequisite

treatment_vs_baseline.treatment: the whole CPP pack (74 skills) installed, per subject.json's select: "all"
treatment_vs_baseline.baseline: an identical disposable home with no skill installed
treatment_vs_baseline.note: each case plans BOTH arms as its own trial (found missing from the cost estimate by cross-model review, #26) - the baseline arm still runs a real, paid agent attempt (it must show no skill invoked, which needs the same live call as the treatment arm), so both count toward the estimate below

repeat_schedule.rationale: a bounded pilot per #26's own resource-bounds section: three cases, one collection, one client configuration, no repeats added until a benefit appears

arm_order: treatment then baseline, per case, matching skillc/materialize.py's existing arm ordering

time_caps.note: not yet enforced by any committed control in this PR - #10's Docker backend Limits (skillc/backend.py) is where this would be wired once #77's implementation lands

monetary_ceiling_source: operator ruling, 2026-09-26 (ADR 0005 rule 6): "don't worry about the cost estimate... i expect it's under $5" - enforced in code by skillc.cost_estimate.authorize. Applies to dollar-metered judge-call spend; this probe enables no judge tier (judge_estimated_quota_usd_equivalent below is 0), so the ceiling is trivially satisfied and no budget approval is required for it.

price.name: gpt-5.1-codex
price.source: pricepertoken.com, 2026-09-26 (third-party aggregator, not independently confirmed against OpenAI's own page)

assumptions.basis: no attempt has ever run against this subject; these are placeholder assumptions (system prompt + CPP skill listing + goal.md for input, agent reasoning/tool calls/patch for output), not measurements. The first live attempt should replace them with observed values. This assumption reads like a single turn and is weak in a specific, known direction: a multi-turn agentic Codex session re-sends its context (including the 74-skill listing) every turn, so real input could be 10-20x higher. Sensitivity, same 6 attempts, expressed at the same public per-token prices purely as a QUOTA indicator (see quota_note): 500,000 input tokens/attempt -> 4.05 quota-usd-equivalent; 1,000,000 input tokens/attempt -> 7.80 quota-usd-equivalent.

cost_estimate.quota_note: NOT a dollar charge (ADR 0005 rule 6): this probe's agent attempts run under the operator's normal Codex subscription login, so this figure is a usage/quota indicator only, computed at public per-token prices for comparability, never billed and never compared against monetary_ceiling_usd.
cost_estimate.judge_note: no judge tier is enabled for this probe - #69's grading tiers are a separate concern from selection-probe's deterministic grading, so there is no dollar-metered judge spend to estimate here.

execution: incomplete - no live run: the agent-quota figure needs no budget approval under ADR 0005 rule 6 (no judge tier is enabled, so judge spend is $0); the in-container credential path for a subscription-login agent run (issue #98) is now built, but skillc/trial.py's real attempt-execution loop does not exist yet
